- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap upward revisions after strong positive sentiment.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) by forecasting further gains — apply lagged mean reversion: if price rises >3% from 5-day avg, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct — force downward adjustment if sentiment drops below 0.3 within 3 days of peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — use 10–15% downward bias if sentiment <0.6.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model overfits short-term momentum — apply smoothing filter: average last 5 days’ sentiment to adjust forecast weight.
